title: Starship Reaches Orbit for First Time, but Returns Early
paragraphs: SpaceX's giant Starship rocket has reached orbit around Earth for the first time. However, the mission ended earlier than planned.

The rocket was launched on September 28, 2026, from Starbase, SpaceX's launch site in Texas. It was Starship's 14th test flight, and the first to complete a full orbit. All of its earlier test flights had been suborbital, meaning they did not go all the way around the Earth.

The flight did not go perfectly. Shortly after launch, the Super Heavy booster, the lower part of the rocket, lost one of its 33 engines, although this did not affect its performance. The booster later made a soft landing in the Gulf of Mexico. Unlike some earlier flights, SpaceX did not try to catch the booster with its launch tower. The Starship spacecraft also lost one of its six engines during the climb. However, SpaceX decided to continue and send the spacecraft into orbit.

Once in orbit, Starship released 26 of SpaceX's latest Starlink internet satellites. According to reports, the new satellites can send down 10 times as much data as the previous version. SpaceX had planned for Starship to circle the Earth six times during a flight lasting nearly 10 hours. However, the company decided to bring the spacecraft back early. It splashed down in the North Pacific Ocean about three hours and eight minutes after launch. SpaceX did not immediately explain why it ended the mission early.
SpaceX celebrated the flight, posting "Starship is orbital." NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman also praised the launch.

The milestone is important for NASA, which plans to use a version of Starship to land astronauts on the Moon. Earlier in 2026, NASA's Artemis II mission carried four astronauts around the Moon. NASA wants to return astronauts to the Moon's surface before January 2029. However, SpaceX still needs to show that it can refuel Starship in space, which will require several more launches.
